scope: Published API v1 POST idempotency and low-level error semantics. This is a contract-derived offline model, not a credentialed live integration.

clauses.statement: A POST sent with an idempotency key may be retried after a network error using the same key and identical parameters without creating a second operation inside the retention window.
The provider returns the first saved status code and response body for an exact replay, including a saved 500 result.
Reusing a key with changed parameters is rejected.
Results are saved only after endpoint execution begins; pre-execution validation failures are retryable and are not modeled as a saved idempotent result.
Keys can be removed after at least 24 hours, so reuse outside the conservative 24-hour window can execute a new operation.
A 500 response remains semantically indeterminate even when its cached response is replayed; later read-back or asynchronous events may reveal side effects.
ClaimSieve additionally requires current authority, exact reservation identity, exact endpoint/account/request binding, and a bounded replay budget before the same transport dispatch may be replayed.
clauses.classification: ClaimSieve design constraint, not a provider guarantee

explicit_nonclaims: No Stripe API credential was used.
No live object, payment, customer, webhook endpoint, or external side effect was created.
The model does not establish behavior outside the cited contract or for provider incidents that violate the published contract.
Webhook delivery, signature verification, event ordering, duplication, and account-context handling are not live-tested in this release.
